title.narrative: Decarbonization of industry and the building Sector in Thailand through the adoption of integrated net-zero and nature-positive solutions

description.narrative: Decarbonization of industry and the building sector reduces significant GHG emissions by 2030, through the adoption of integrated climate-compatible and nature-positive solutions.
Note: Disbursement data provided is cumulative and covers disbursement made by the project Agency.

The proposed project in Thailand, focused on implementing a climate-just NZNP approach with a specific emphasis on the industry and building sector, holds the potential to deliver significant socioeconomic benefits. At the national level, the project aims to enhance the development and implementation of NZNPA integrated NDC targets and goals for industrial sectors and integrate green economy sectors into policy frameworks, ensuring consistency with global climate change mitigation and biodiversity conservation framework objectives. This integration, supported by the GEF, promotes sustainable development by aligning economic growth with environmental and climate goals. Additionally, GEF's financial assistance addresses systemic challenges, facilitating the unlocking of mechanisms for decarbonization and contributing to economy-wide reduction of carbon emissions and biodiversity conservation and nature positive outcomes. The project establishes a coordination platform that fosters collaboration among government, industrial, and societal stakeholders. This localized approach ensures a holistic and community-engaged strategy for decarbonization and biodiversity preservation. Capacity building, demonstrations, and policy implementation at the local level contribute to the creation of skilled jobs, innovation, and improved practices within the industry and building sectors. The promotion of nature-positive materials in construction not only reduces embodied carbon emissions but also stimulates local innovation and business opportunities. This local engagement aligns with GEF's focus on empowering communities and contributes to adaptation by enhancing resilience and adaptive capacity. Economic benefits arise both because of direct and indirect cost savings due to reduced waste disposal, resource and energy consumption, sustainable sourcing and utilization of raw materials and increased competitiveness. In addition, skills improvement, training, technology transfer, positive image, branding, and the effects of applying best practices bring indirect job creation. The creation of local jobs especially has a positive social impact when it properly incorporates aspects of gender equality and youth empowerment. Reduced air pollution and emissions, preservation and protection of biodiversity and nature, and more efficient use of resources provide clear and measurable environmental benefits. The project broadly supports and encourages entrepreneurs that develops innovative local carbon technologies and supports inclusivity by dedicated attention to women entrepreneurs working in the space and support opportunities for women to work in the labour market in Thailand. From a gender perspective, the project also supports development of safe, clean and efficient industrial and construction sector for men and women, in turn supporting economic growth by working in good and safe working environment, instilling confidence and offering new skills and technical capacity. Overall, the project's comprehensive strategy, supported by GEF funds, addresses both national and local socioeconomic dimensions. It not only facilitates the integration of green and climate-conscious policies but also empowers local communities to actively participate in and adapt to the global challenges of climate change. The project's alignment with GEF objectives positions it as a catalyst for sustainable development, decarbonization, and biodiversity preservation at multiple levels.
